# Accessibility Standards (Compact)

Use this guide as the default quality bar for web UI changes.

## Severity

- **CRITICAL**: Blocks access. Must be fixed before merge.
- **IMPORTANT**: Major barrier. Fix in the same sprint.
- **SUGGESTION**: Improves usability. Plan soon.

## Compliance Target

- Ship to **WCAG 2.2 AA**.
- This covers current legal baselines (WCAG 2.1/2.0 AA requirements).
- Keep in mind current enforcement context:
  - EAA (EU, enforced since 2025)
  - ADA Title II digital rule (US, 2026+)
  - Section 508 (US federal baseline)

## Non-Negotiable Rules

### Structure and semantics

- Set document language (`<html lang="...">`).
- Use landmarks (`<header>`, `<nav>`, `<main>`, `<footer>`).
- Keep heading order logical (`h1 > h2 > h3`, no gaps).
- Prefer native controls (`<button>`, `<a>`, `<input>`) over clickable divs/spans.
- Ensure data tables include headers (`<th>` + proper scope/caption).

### Names, labels, and instructions

- Every interactive element needs an accessible name.
- Every form control needs a visible label or explicit ARIA labeling.
- Do not use placeholder as the only label.
- Link inline errors to fields with `aria-describedby`; set `aria-invalid`.

### Keyboard and focus

- All functionality must be keyboard operable.
- No keyboard traps; overlays must close with Escape unless essential.
- Preserve meaningful focus order.
- Keep visible focus styles (`:focus-visible`); do not remove outline without replacement.
- Return focus to trigger (or best logical element) when dialogs close.
- Include a skip link to main content.

### Visual and media

- Text contrast: 4.5:1 normal, 3:1 large.
- Non-text contrast (icons/borders/focus): 3:1.
- Do not convey meaning with color alone.
- Support reflow down to 320px without horizontal reading scroll.
- Respect `prefers-reduced-motion` for non-essential motion.
- Informational images require `alt`; decorative images use `alt=""`.
- Prerecorded video needs captions.

### Dynamic content and SPA behavior

- Announce async status/errors (`role="status"`, `role="alert"`, or `aria-live`).
- Ensure route changes are announced (title and heading updates).

## Five Rules of ARIA

1. Prefer native HTML before ARIA.
2. Do not override native semantics incorrectly.
3. ARIA widgets must be fully keyboard operable.
4. Never put `aria-hidden="true"` on focusable elements.
5. All interactive controls need an accessible name.

## High-Value Anti-Patterns

| ID | Severity | Detect | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | CRITICAL | Missing `<html lang>` | Add correct page language |
| S4 | IMPORTANT | No landmarks | Use semantic page regions |
| S6 | CRITICAL | Data table missing headers | Add `<th>`, scope, caption |
| S8 | CRITICAL | `onClick` on div/span | Use native button/link |
| A2 | CRITICAL | Focusable + `aria-hidden="true"` | Remove focusability or hidden state |
| A3 | CRITICAL | ARIA role missing required states | Add required role attributes |
| A6 | CRITICAL | Icon-only button without name | Add visible text or `aria-label` |
| K2 | CRITICAL | Positive `tabindex` | Use only `0` or `-1` |
| K5 | CRITICAL | `outline: none` with no replacement | Add strong `:focus-visible` style |
| F1 | CRITICAL | Input missing label | Add `<label>` or ARIA labeling |
| F2 | CRITICAL | Error text not linked to field | Use `aria-describedby` + `aria-invalid` |
| V1 | CRITICAL | Low text contrast | Raise contrast to AA threshold |
| V2 | CRITICAL | Color-only feedback | Add text/icon/border signal |
| D1 | CRITICAL | Image missing `alt` | Add meaningful alt or empty alt |
| D3 | CRITICAL | Video without captions | Add caption track |

## Framework Notes

### React / Next.js

- Use `htmlFor` in JSX labels.
- Ensure unique page titles and route announcements.
- When conditional UI re-renders, preserve or restore focus intentionally.
- Sanitize and structurally validate injected HTML.

### Angular

- Avoid `(click)` on non-interactive elements unless full role + keyboard support is added.
- Use CDK dialog/focus tools for modals (`cdkTrapFocus` or `Dialog`).
- Announce route changes with `LiveAnnouncer`.
- Bind validation state to `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`.

### Vue

- Avoid `@click` on non-interactive elements unless full keyboard semantics are present.
- Manage focus after `v-if` toggles (`nextTick` + focus target).
- Sanitize and structure-check any `v-html` content.

## Keyboard Expectations

- `Tab` / `Shift+Tab`: move through focus order.
- `Enter` / `Space`: activate controls as expected.
- `Escape`: dismiss dialogs/popovers/menus when allowed.
- Arrow keys/Home/End: navigate composite widgets (tabs, menus, listboxes, trees).

## Minimum Review Checklist

- [ ] Semantics: language, landmarks, heading order, native controls
- [ ] Names/labels: controls named, fields labeled, errors linked
- [ ] Keyboard: full operability, no traps, visible focus, skip link
- [ ] Visual: AA contrast, no color-only meaning, responsive reflow
- [ ] Media: image alt text, captioned video
- [ ] Dynamic updates: status announced, SPA navigation announced
- [ ] ARIA: valid roles/states only, no redundant or conflicting usage

## Practical Default

If unsure, choose the native semantic element, keep keyboard support first-class, and verify with:

1. Keyboard-only navigation
2. Screen reader smoke test
3. Contrast check
4. Narrow viewport (320px)
